solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relative needing car upholstered

indicators.note: to upholster is to stuff and rework a seat, so the letters of the two words are packed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's family member needs the seats in their car re-covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upholstered' rearranges the ten letters of NEEDING and CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's granddaughter is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Decline fight after live turns

indicators.note: after places the fight word behind the turned live word
turns means the word for live is read backwards

parts.note: to live is to be
a bout is a boxing fight

explanation.surface: A boxer's career declines after life takes a turn for the worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' is a verb here, as in a tide going out; 'turns' acts on 'live' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb out is to recede or dwindle away, as a tide does, so to decline.

clue.text: To cut to the chase in this, deranged Old Nick's here

definitions.text: To cut to the chase in this

parts.note: deranged means crazy, nuts
Old Nick is the Devil, whose home is hell

explanation.surface: A mad remark that the Devil lives here, put bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'in a nutshell': putting something briefly is cutting to the chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in brief, summarised form is putting it in a nutshell, which is getting straight to the point.

clue.text: Accepting lecturer that is not doing anything

indicators.note: accepting means the words for that is take the lecturer letter inside them

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A lecturer agrees that he is lazy, doing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: ID EST is the full Latin behind the abbreviation i.e.; L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of idle describes whoever is most inactive, the one doing nothing whatever.

clue.text: Rufus anagrams cut out, right?

indicators.note: anagrams is used as a verb here: the word Rufus anagrams, so its letters are reordered
out means the letters of cut are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Rufus's word puzzles have been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'anagrams' rearranges RUFUS to USUFR, and 'out' rearranges CUT to UCT.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal term names the right to use and profit from another's property while leaving it undamaged.

clue.text: Suspect Spock's lead, overpowering Enterprise, say

indicators.note: in a down answer, overpowering puts the first piece on top of the second
lead means the first letter of the word Spock

parts.note: the starship Enterprise in Star Trek bears the prefix USS, as a United States ship

explanation.surface: Mr Spock, the science officer, takes control of the starship Enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Enterprise is the Star Trek ship USS Enterprise; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to suss something is to work it out or sense it, so to suspect.

clue.text: Bird and horse in a flash united

indicators.note: in places the horse inside the word for a flash

parts.note: a mo, short for moment, is a flash of time
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A bird and a horse joined together in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flash' looks like one phrase, but 'a flash' alone is MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The marabou is a large African stork, a bird.

clue.text: Potentially "trim" "Ladies' Man" to be a bad manager

indicators.note: potentially means these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A smart ladies' man could make a poor boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' rearranges the letters of TRIM and LADIES MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer badly is to mismanage, the behaviour of a poor manager.

clue.text: Interrupt periods of sexual excitement, tender, massaging back

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled piece is read in reverse
massaging means the tender word wraps around and rubs the periods word, holding it inside

parts.note: to tender is to offer, to bid
ruts are the seasonal mating periods of deer

explanation.surface: A tender back massage gets interrupted at a moment of arousal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' is a verb (to offer, as at an auction), not soft or loving; 'back' reverses the whole assembly, BRUTSID.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to interrupt them in what they are doing.

clue.text: You won't get sent down with it

definitions.text: You won't get sent down with it

parts.words: You won't get sent down with it
parts.note: sent down is British slang for jailed; a person free of fault won't be imprisoned

explanation.walkthrough: Sent down here means sent to prison, not expelled or sent downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom from fault or guilt means no court can send a person to jail.

clue.text: In a way, received accepted American seafood

indicators.note: In means the following pieces sit inside the word for a way

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: accepted means the received word takes the American abbreviation inside it

parts.note: received means got

explanation.surface: An American is served seafood they accepted, in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: US goes into GOT for GOUST, which goes into LANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiny lobster eaten as shellfish, the French name used on menus.

clue.text: Bottom of Western pit?

indicators.note: in an across answer, westward means read right to left, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: ass is American slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A query about the deepest part of a mine in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' reverses ASS OF; it works only in an across clue, which runs west to east.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy this is a shallow depression or hollow, a pit.

clue.text: What calms Homer's rage?

parts.note: Homer Simpson of the cartoon The Simpsons is soothed by a sweet ring-shaped snack; to do one's nut is British slang for to rage

explanation.walkthrough: Homer is Homer Simpson, not the Greek poet; 'do one's nut' is British slang for flying into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The American spelling of the fried ring cake that Homer Simpson famously loves.

clue.text: They follow the same generation as us after 10, getting hammered

indicators.note: after places the generation words behind the jumbled number
getting hammered means beaten out of shape, so the letters of the number are jumbled

parts.note: the numeral 10 is the word ten
people of our own generation are of our age

explanation.surface: Our peers after ten o'clock, getting very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is the number ten, not a reference to 10-across; 'getting hammered' scrambles it into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of attendants or hangers-on who trail after an important person.

clue.text: What EULC should give retort, rudely?

definitions.meaning: EULC is the word clue written backwards, so its solution should come back the other way too
to reply impertinently, especially to a parent or teacher

explanation.walkthrough: EULC is CLUE reversed; the solution to a clue written backwards would be its answer, back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Replying cheekily to someone in authority is a rude retort.

clue.text: In the cold I've cracked up bad outside dodgy cafe

definitions.text: In the cold I've cracked up

indicators.note: outside means the word for bad wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: bad means ill, unwell

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or broken, so the letters of cafe are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone freezing, ill and broken down outside a shady cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a person cracking up from cold; it describes a glacier. 'dodgy' gives CEFA.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep broken section of a glacier, where the ice is cracked into blocks in the cold.

clue.text: Self-important claim briefly covers name

indicators.note: covers means the shortened claim word wraps around the name letter
briefly means the claim word loses its last letter

parts.note: to arrogate is to claim without right

explanation.surface: A pompous person's claim, put briefly, hides a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts ARROGATE to ARROGAT, which 'covers' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughty and overbearing, full of an exaggerated sense of one's own importance.

clue.text: Entertainer is tense putting across talent with energy

indicators.note: putting across means the talent word is set before, with is and tense following it across the grid

parts.note: art is skill or talent
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A performer grows tense while conveying their gift with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: ART is followed by IS and T, then E; 'with' simply joins the energy piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional performer, such as a singer or dancer, is an entertainer.

clue.text: A toy has to soften up Achates

indicators.note: has means the toy holds the reversed soften word inside it

parts.note: Lego is a construction toy

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to ret is to soften flax by soaking

explanation.surface: A toy has to be broken in by softening.
explanation.walkthrough: Retting is soaking flax to soften its fibres; 'up' gives TER. Achates is the faithful friend of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates is the classic loyal companion, a trusted second self.

clue.text: One approaching his family with some seriousness

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
approaching means near
a nest is a bird's brood of young, its family

explanation.surface: Someone nearing his relatives with a solemn air.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting sincerely and seriously, rather than in jest.

clue.text: Shun women after artist

indicators.note: after means the women letter comes at the tail of the artist, in place of his final letter

parts.note: M. C. Escher was the Dutch graphic artist of impossible staircases

explanation.surface: A command to avoid women who follow a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist is M. C. Escher; W takes the place of his final R, a step the clue leaves loosely signalled by 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to avoid or abstain from it deliberately.

clue.text: On board, game woman with title deserts some European

indicators.note: deserts means the European word leaves the titled woman

parts.note: a duchess is a woman with a noble title
du is French for some, as in du pain

explanation.surface: A titled lady abandons her European companions to play a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: DU is French for 'some' (a European's word for it); it leaves DUCHESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy game for two played with pieces on a chequered board.

clue.text: The peasant's too near the knuckle, getting a lift?

indicators.note: getting means the vehicle word receives the other piece inside it

parts.note: giving someone a lift means taking them by car
OTT stands for over the top, too extreme, as is something near the knuckle

explanation.surface: A peasant's joke goes too far, so somebody drives him off.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is short for 'over the top'; the 's after 'peasant' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish farm tenant or labourer who rented a cottage, a type of peasant.

clue.text: Obsession article

definitions.meaning: a fixation, as in having a ... about someone

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday uses: a fixation, and any physical item or object.

clue.text: What's written up to you in French letter

indicators.note: in a down answer, written up means the phrase is read from bottom to top

parts.note: French for to you is a toi

explanation.surface: A query about what goes into a French letter written for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French letter' is slang for a condom, but here 'French' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Bridge playing here, warranting caution, takes time

indicators.note: takes means the caution word holds the time letter inside

parts.note: in football an offence earning a yellow card, or caution, is cardable

explanation.surface: Bridge players need to watch it, as the game takes time.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a booking is a caution, shown with a yellow card, so a cautionable foul is CARDABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folding table on which card games such as bridge are played.

clue.text: On return, poet's always one boarding train

indicators.note: On return means the whole piece is read backwards
boarding means the one word gets inside the always word, like a passenger

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
a unit is one

explanation.surface: A poet always comes back to board the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway train but means a following of attendants; 'On return' reverses EUNITER.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is the group of attendants following a dignitary, the same sense as a train of followers.

clue.text: Looks new in candies

indicators.note: in means the new letter goes inside the candies word

parts.note: to glacé fruit is to candy it, so candies is glacés

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the new sweets with interest.
explanation.walkthrough: Candies is a verb here: glacés is French-derived for candies or ices with sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick peeks or glimpses are brief looks.
